industries.intro: We make public health, education and civic campaigns with the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, which represents 21 tribal nations. The lesson every time: do the research first, then let community members tell their own stories.

hard.p: Many communities have good reason to doubt outside campaigns. Our research looks for that history first, so the film speaks to it instead of around it.
Leaders, elders, mothers and young voters speak for themselves. No outside narrator, no institutional voice.
We film where people live and work, and we ask before we point a camera at anything.

faq.a: Yes. Our work for the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona includes WIC nutrition PSAs, vaccine education for its Tribal Epidemiology Center and Your Voice, Your Power, a 10-part docuseries on tribal voting.

faq.q: What does a SITREP add to a tribal campaign?
faq.a: It finds the real barrier before we film. For ITCA's WIC program, the research showed the problem was trust, not awareness, and that changed the whole creative direction.

cases.title: Dear Mom
cases.text: Tribal mothers speaking straight to other mothers, so families trust WIC enough to enroll.
cases.story: The Inter Tribal Council of Arizona's WIC program had eligible families who weren't enrolling. Our SITREP found the barrier was trust, not awareness, so we put tribal mothers on camera talking straight to other mothers: no narration, no institutional voice, shot in unbroken takes so they read as neighbors.

sitrep: ITCA needed more WIC enrollment. Participation was declining even though families were eligible.

Tribal mothers speaking straight to camera, shot in unbroken takes. No narration, no institutional framing.
